---
title: "02_meta_clean"
format: html
---

Step 1: Load the packages to be used.

```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
```

Step 2: Dive into the composition and content of the metadata set, as it relates to clinical annotations.

```{r}
# Load the metadata from the tsv file
metadata <- read_tsv(here("data", "01_meta_load.tsv"))

# Inspect the available clinical fields (columns)
names(metadata)

# Look at the sample's descriptive columns and identify the type and distribution of their values
metadata[, grep("characteristics|title|source",
             names(metadata), ignore.case = TRUE),
     drop = FALSE]

```

Step 3: Create a clean metadata tibble.

```{r}
#Create metadata_clean with metadata as a basis, retaining the relevant columns and transforming them as needed.
metadata_clean <- metadata |>
  transmute(
    sample_id,
    original_group = str_extract(title, "Group [1-4]"),
    age = as.numeric(`age:ch1`),
    smoking_pack_years = as.numeric(`smoking pack/yr:ch1`),

    baseline_ffpe_raw = `bl ffpe dx:ch1`,
    baseline_frozen_raw = `bl frozen dx:ch1`,
    followup_raw = `f/u bx dx:ch1`
  ) |>
  mutate(
    baseline_ffpe = as.integer(
      str_extract(baseline_ffpe_raw, "^[1-7]")
    ),
    baseline_frozen = as.integer(
      str_extract(baseline_frozen_raw, "^[1-7]")
    ),
    followup = as.integer(followup_raw),

    ffpe_angiogenic = str_detect(
      baseline_ffpe_raw, "\\.1$"
    ),
    frozen_angiogenic = str_detect(
      baseline_frozen_raw, "\\.1$"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#We drop 
metadata_clean <- metadata_clean |>
  select(
    -baseline_ffpe_raw,
    -baseline_frozen_raw,
    -followup_raw
  )
```

Step 4: Inspect metadata_clean and check that the transformations worked

```{r}

# Inspect the resulting dataset
head(metadata_clean)

# Check group sizes from the original titles
table(metadata_clean$original_group)

# Check missingness in the relevant variables
colSums(is.na(metadata_clean))

# Examine discrepancies between the baseline diagnoses
metadata_clean |>
  filter(
    !is.na(baseline_ffpe),
    baseline_ffpe != baseline_frozen
  ) |>
  select(
    sample_id,
    original_group,
    baseline_ffpe,
    baseline_frozen
  )

```

The produced metadata_clean set contains 63 samples, with the expected distribution across the four clinical outcome groups, which provides a basic level that the study's information was retained after the cleaning process. Other than that, there are three important observations to be extracted from its inspection:

-   Only `baseline_ffpe` contains one missing value. The raw column has no missing values because `"ND"` is a recorded string, but it becomes `NA` when we extract a numeric histological grade.

-   11 of the 63 samples have different FFPE and frozen baseline grades. That's about 17.5% of the observations. However, all 11 differences are just one histological grade apart.

-   These discrepancies don't represent contradictory clinical classifications**.** None crosses the boundary between nondysplastic (grades 1–2) and dysplastic (grades 4–7).

Step 5: Reconstruct the groups presented in the article

We reconstruct the clinical outcome group classifications ourselves using the clinical variables to validate the dataset further and reproduce the publication's results.\
The histological scores are translated to classes as follows:

| Histological score | Classification      |
|--------------------|---------------------|
| 1–2                | Nondysplastic       |
| 3                  | Squamous metaplasia |
| 4–7                | Dysplastic          |

In order to be consistent with the two score 3 follow-up observations assigned to the regression group in the dataset, scores of 3 will be grouped with the nondysplastic outcomes.

```{r}
metadata_clean <- metadata_clean |>
  mutate(
    baseline_status = case_when(
      baseline_frozen %in% 1:2 ~ "Nondysplastic",
      baseline_frozen %in% 4:7 ~ "Dysplastic",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    followup_status = case_when(
      followup %in% 1:3 ~ "Nondysplastic",
      followup %in% 4:7 ~ "Dysplastic",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
metadata_clean <- metadata_clean |>
  mutate(
    reconstructed_group = case_when(
      baseline_status == "Dysplastic" &
        followup_status == "Dysplastic" ~ "Group 1",

      baseline_status == "Dysplastic" &
        followup_status == "Nondysplastic" ~ "Group 2",

      baseline_status == "Nondysplastic" &
        followup_status == "Dysplastic" ~ "Group 3",

      baseline_status == "Nondysplastic" &
        followup_status == "Nondysplastic" ~ "Group 4",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

To validate the group reconstruction is correct, we produce the following table:

```{r}
table(
  Original = metadata_clean$original_group,
  Reconstructed = metadata_clean$reconstructed_group,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
```

So we prove that the reconstructed classification matches the published groups for all 63 observations.

Step 6: Save the cleaned dataset in the `data` folder.

```{r}
write_tsv(
  metadata_clean,
  here("data", "02_clean_metadata.tsv")
)
```
